scenes.description: Nathan Black lingers in the lecture hall after his classmates have left. Jackson and David approach him, curious about his thoughts on the class. The atmosphere is quiet but charged with unspoken tension as Nathan grapples with his uncertain future.

characters.position: Sitting on the edge of a desk

actions.dialogue: Hey Nathan, you stayed behind after the lecture. You okay? You looked like you had a lot on your mind.
Yeah... I just need some time to process. I'm not sure if I'm on the right track anymore.
Maybe you're not wrong to question it. Tech and business aren't mutually exclusive. I think there's a lot of value in combining both.
But you're one of the best in the class. Why even think about leaving it behind?
I love tech, but I'm starting to see how business can give it more purpose. I want to make an impact, not just code for the sake of it.
That makes sense. Have you considered a dual major or maybe an internship in the business department? It could help you explore both fields.
I haven't, but maybe it's worth looking into. I just don't want to lose touch with what I love about tech.

scenes.plot: Nathan is struggling with the decision to shift his focus from technology to business. His friends Jackson and David confront him with their perspectives, challenging and supporting him in his journey of self-exploration.
scenes.social_purpose: To naturally reveal Nathan's internal conflict and values through a conversation with his peers, while also showing how their differing interests and personalities influence the discussion.

chunk.text: Nathan's contemplative nature and uncertainty are evident as he weighs his options. Jackson's enthusiasm for technology contrasts with David's more balanced view of combining tech and business. Their dialogue highlights Nathan's analytical approach and his desire to plan for a meaningful future.
